profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC22 data center at 22165 Beaumeade Circle in Ashburn, Virginia, one node in Equinix's cluster of buildings spread across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC22 facility page does not publish the square footage or power redundancy figures it lists for several sibling buildings on this same campus, showing a placeholder that directs prospective customers to contact sales for those specifications, so this entry does not report a footprint or an IT load in megawatts for DC22. The one distinguishing fact Equinix does confirm publicly for DC22 is that the building's power is described as 100 percent covered by renewable energy, a sustainability claim the company highlights on the DC22 page alongside a general reference to high density cooling capability, without further technical detail beyond that.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival on Beaumeade Circle. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed. Equinix opened its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second building, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group of buildings, and DC22 itself is described on Equinix's site in general terms, as a newer and highly interconnected building on the campus, without the specific customer base or cross connect counts Equinix sometimes discloses for older facilities in the group.

Every building on this campus, including DC22, now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, requiring large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

reading.body:
Equinix DC22 sits in Ashburn, Virginia as one of fifteen buildings Equinix operates across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, but the operator does not publish the facility's power capacity, square footage, or IT load. The building's single disclosed distinguishing fact is that Equinix states its power comes from 100 percent renewable energy sources. Without published megawatt figures, DC22 cannot be ranked or sized against other facilities in the region.

Ashburn has become the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet of built infrastructure, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own DC1 and DC2 buildings from the late 1990s. The entire Data Center Alley corridor consumes on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide across all operators. Virginia as a state has 330 mapped data center facilities and 25 facilities with published power figures, totaling 1,603 megawatts, with Equinix's Ashburn campus ranking 26th by published megawatts, though that ranking reflects only the subset of Equinix's fifteen buildings in the region for which the operator has disclosed individual power figures.

As of January 1, 2027, every building on this campus now operates under Virginia's new GS-5 rate class for data centers, which requires large demand customers like Equinix to sign 14-year minimum contracts with Dominion Energy under cost coverage guarantees approved by the State Corporation Commission in November 2026. This regulatory shift locks in long-term electricity terms for any AI infrastructure Equinix may site in DC22, but does not change the fact that DC22's actual power consumption and effective hosting capacity remain unpublished.
